incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-43871 fired for service/aggregator latency_p95 > 1200ms (3m) :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: PD-43871 assigned to oncall -> Maya :bell:
Maya: ack'd PD-43871 - looking into it now, tagging Ravi in case it needs infra help
Ravi: on stand-by, pulling metrics and logs. can someone paste a spike graph?
Emily: here — dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/agg/latency?range=5m shows short 30s spike around now, not sustained
Maya: running `kubectl logs -n prod aggregator-pod-7f9 | tail -n 200` — seeing a series of transient `rpc timeout` and `connection reset` entries, looks like a burst of upstream retries
Maya: also noticed route table churn in router-2: `conn_count` jumped from 120 -> 600 then back down in ~40s
Ravi: checking infra nodes, GPU hosts healthy, no OOM. network metrics show a short BGP flap in us-west-2 at t+00:00:28
Emily: customer impact? any 5xx visible?
Maya: quick sweep of logs: 502s up for ~8 requests across multiple tenants. not customer-facing degraded, errors are internal-retryable. marking P2 for now
SRE Manager: if it auto-resolves and impact remains negligible, we can close as noisy transient; but capture runbook steps so we don't re-alert
Maya: creating a short runbook note: "PD-43871 — ephemeral aggregator latency surge due to transient upstream net churn; steps taken: ack, check node health, verify kv/cache warmup, check router conn counts, monitor for repeat"
Ravi: I enabled a 60s suppression on the PD rule for `service/aggregator latency_p95` to avoid flap loop while we observe — will revert if we see continued issues :thumbsup:
pagerduty-bot: PD-43871 status -> acknowledged by Maya
incident-bot: Alert auto-resolved (PD-43871) — condition cleared after 78s :white_check_mark:
Maya: confirmed metrics returned to baseline, tail of logs shows normal request latency and no lingering retries
Emily: re-checking synthetic probes, all green now. no customer-reported incidents in #support in past 15m
Ravi: leaving a note to follow up with networking to see if the BGP micro-flap is correlated with a scheduled maintenance window in us-west-2
SRE Manager: good — mark as autoresolved, add to weekly noisy-alerts triage. if similar pattern repeats, we'll increase the aggregation window or tweak alert sensitivity
Maya: closing PD and thread. PD-43871 -> resolved by system after suppression window. will add short blameless note to the incident board. :sparkles:
